[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Validate and display %wait agent-tribe references correctly[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]A `%wait(@<tribe>)` target is understood end to end: reserved [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]pseudo-tribe references such as `@default` are rejected at launch [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]instead of parking an agent forever, and the ACE Agents tab renders[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]a real tribe wait as a pending-or-bound tribe target instead of a [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]missing agent name.[/#D7D7AF]

[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Reject reserved tribe references in wait and fork targets[/bold #D7AFFF]     [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]reserved-tribe-guard[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]reserved-tribe-guard: add a canonical reserved-tribe concept to core and[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]reject `@default` (and any other reserved pseudo-tribe) wherever a tribe[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]reference is used as a `%wait` or `#fork` target, so the launch fails [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]with a clear message instead of parking forever.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Shared tribe wait binding resolver[/bold #D7AFFF]                            [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]tribe-wait-binding[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]tribe-wait-binding: extract the `tribe_candidate` ordering and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]aggregation rules into a pure, snapshot-driven resolver in Python core [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]that both the wait index and the TUI can call, and add a [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]pending/bound/reserved classification the display layer can consume [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]without touching disk.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Tribe-aware wait rendering in the Agents tab[/bold #D7AFFF]                  [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]ace-tribe-wait-display[dim] · [dim][/dim]after tribe-wait-binding[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]ace-tribe-wait-display: stop classifying tribe wait targets as missing [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]agent names, give them their own wait lane tag and tribe identity [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]styling, show the bound entity and its status once one exists, and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]refresh the affected render-cache keys, help text, and PNG snapshots.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Surface waits that can never resolve[/bold #D7AFFF]                          [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]unresolvable-wait-surface[dim] · [dim][/dim]after reserved-tribe-guard, [/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#AF87FF][dim]ace-tribe-wait-display[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]unresolvable-wait-surface: give already-parked reserved-tribe waits a [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]distinct "this wait can never resolve" presentation in ACE so agents [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]launched before the guard landed are diagnosable rather than silently [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]pending.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
